Theme 073 · Characters & mascots

Living Widgets

Every dashboard widget is a tiny character with googly eyes. Nobody is watching them, so they doze and stare in all directions — until Pulse arrives and every widget turns to look. The checkout card physically slumps when it breaks; you press the button.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Eyed widget — any chart card + two googly eyes; pupil direction = attention
  • Sleep eyes — closed arcs = an unwatched dashboard (the pain)
  • Hero card — the one anomalous metric, scaled up, with brows and a sweat drop
  • Anomaly readout — −18% in coral + mono meta line (since 09:42 · deploy #2231)
  • Decision pill — coral Roll back + ghost Acknowledge, pressed by a real cursor
  • Happy row — the widget cast lined up with smiling eyes under the CTA

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Pupil snap — pupils tween to a look-at target in 0.12 s power4.out, 20 ms stagger; always on a downbeat (every 0.5 s at 120 BPM)
  • Slump & squash — hero card rotates to −3° with a 6 % vertical squash, 0.4 s back.out(2); the break in the line is drawn over one beat
  • Idle blink — each widget blinks (scaleY 1→0.1→1, 0.14 s) at random 2–4 bar intervals; blinks are quantised to 8ths so the wall pulses with the hi-hat

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Why: Faces make an abstract monitoring product legible in half a second: eyes pointing at the problem are a built-in arrow, and 'nobody is watching your dashboards' becomes literal. Luxo-style posture (slump, tilt) carries emotion without dialogue. Risk: Cute can read as childish for enterprise buyers — keep the UI itself real and restrained, put personality only in eyes and posture, and never give the widgets mouths or voices.

Adapt to your product: Use your own dashboard cards, charts or table rows as the cast; keep the eyes the only addition. Your key metric becomes the hero card and your primary action becomes the button it looks at.

References: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luxo_Jr. (objects carry emotion through posture and timing) · https://www.creativereview.co.uk/mailchimp-rebrand-by-collins/ (SaaS brand character used with restraint (Freddie's wink))
